notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. The upstream OceanScale simulator, its CUDA/Newton/Warp stack and the sim backend were not run: the clone requires Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA 12.8+ and pulls CUDA-enabled wheels (README.md:14-20, pyproject.toml:27-30). The clone registers no gymnasium.make id, so env_id is null and only the fake backend is configured. fake.py is a fresh pure-Python stand-in for oceanscale.rov_env:ROVEnv, not a copy of the exemplar and not the upstream environment; it uses a kinematic acceleration and linear drag (placeholders) instead of Tier-1 hydrodynamics, returns one flat 26-vector and a scalar reward where upstream step always returns batched (n_envs, 26) arrays (constructor default n_envs=64, rov_env.py:346-347), and omits the upstream unseeded Gaussian sensor noise (rov_env.py:768-769), which is why the fidelity determinism is statistical while the fake itself is deterministic for a seed. The fake was not compared with a real upstream run. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for inputs the bridge derives (reset seed, seed input, ticks and the action.values array). Only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
